title: REASSEMBLE Contact-Event and Sensor Recovery
public_source_lookup_gate: explicitly waived by user; not claimed passed

master_archive_range_access.note: The master data.zip content endpoint honors exact byte ranges. Individual member endpoints return complete uncompressed HDF5 files and ignore Range.

first_native_record.sensor_validity: Measured and compensated 3-axis force/torque arrays are finite and timestamp-aligned in the inspected record.
first_native_record.important_scale_warning: The smallest recording has only one substantive action; member count or byte count cannot be used as a proxy for usable action-row yield.

pilot_subset.purpose: One smallest complete recording per day, extracted from the official ZIP with size and CRC verification.

compact_source_capacity.selection_policy: one smallest unchanged HDF5 per collection day, then globally smallest remaining members
compact_source_capacity.finding: A compact unchanged-member source package leaves only a handful of independent hidden recording families; crops do not add independent families.

narration_attack.method: offline openai/whisper-tiny.en on the two fixed microphones
narration_attack.finding: Object identity and action order are audible in every pilot recording, so narrated audio substantially discloses the proposed action/event labels.

audio_redundancy_attack.method: 10 ms log-RMS envelope cross-correlation and least-squares waveform copy
audio_redundancy_attack.finding: Exact waveform recovery is phase-underdetermined, while coarse envelope recovery is strongly shortcuttable by another fixed microphone.

sensor_interpolation_attack.method: linear interpolation between visible endpoints of event-centered masked spans
sensor_interpolation_attack.finding: Correlation-only sequence scoring would over-reward interpolation even though standardized error remains poor.

novelty.closest_source_task: REASSEMBLE multimodal temporal action segmentation and success/anomaly detection
closest_local_clusters: Real Robot Handover Command Timeline Reconstruction
Laundry Resource-State Reconstruction From Sound and Vibration
novelty.finding: The proposal combines existing dense sequence inpainting and event-ledger solution families on a new domain rather than introducing a materially new learning object.

rejection_reasons: novelty score 3.5/10 is below the required 6/10 threshold
operator narration directly discloses action and object labels
exact audio waveform recovery is underdetermined but envelope recovery is cross-microphone shortcuttable
compact unchanged-source packages leave too few independent hidden recording families
success labels have an 88.66% unconditional prior

bounded_salvage.result: Dropping audio/action labels leaves a standard masked force/torque reconstruction task close to existing work; dropping sensor recovery leaves the source's canonical segmentation task. Neither stays within the brief and reaches the novelty threshold.

unresolved_gates: full post-filter count for a compact subset was not pursued after decisive rejection
final metric null-head tests were not implemented after decisive rejection
platform import of the full 58.9 GB archive was not attempted
